messages:
ana: Heads-up — we've got sustained GPU contention in dedicated-pool eu-west-1c this morning. One tenant's batch jobs spiked and pushed multiple small jobs into soft eviction; 95th pct token latency ~3x.
priya: link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/pool/dedicated-eu-west-1c?panel=gpu_utilization — you can see the single host pegged at 98% GPU mem for ~12m.
sam: quick dump from the node:
```
# kubectl top pods -n dedicated-tenant-7
NAME                                   GPU(cores)   GPU(MEM)
batch-job-7-abc                        1/1          100% (24Gi)
small-infer-2                          1/1          12%  (3Gi)
small-infer-3                          1/1          10%  (2.8Gi)
```
And dmesg had repeated "GPU memory allocation failed" traces around 03:14 UTC.
josh: is this the same tenant that caused the noisy-slice alert last month or a new one? Could be workload change (longer sequences).
ana: I think new tenant, but same pattern: heavy single-job memory footprint with no batching-friendly shape.
priya: we should avoid hard evicting small customers. Proposal: add a soft-threshold at 85% GPU mem that triggers request-level throttling and async migration to a "burst" dedicated pool.
sam: +1. Also consider enforcing per-tenant GPU mem quota via cgroup/gpu-slice so one job can't claim entire card. That buys headroom for small tenants.
josh: config idea (pseudo):
```
noisy_neighbor_protection:
  threshold_pct: 85
  action: throttle_then_migrate
  migrate_to: dedicated-burst-pool
  throttle_policy: token_bucket(rate=50rps, burst=200)
```
lee: sounds fine, but migrating to a burst-dedicated pool adds cost if we spin up extra instances. How much are we expecting this to bump monthly?
ana: short term: minimal — we can use existing autoscaler capacity by tagging nodes as burst-eligible and prefer evicting batch jobs with preemption hints. Long term: if this pattern persists we'd need additional reserved commits.
priya: another lever is route-level model fallback: route requests from small tenants to a quantized/cheaper variant when tail latency risk is detected. Lower quality but avoids full eviction.
sam: also re: KV cache: we should ensure dedicated-pool tenants have isolated cache namespaces so caching contention doesn't magnify memory pressure.
josh: agree. For now action items: 1) sam to prototype soft-threshold throttler and cgroup limit (ETA 4 hrs), 2) priya to add route-level fallback for small tenants (ETA EOD), 3) ana to run one-off migration to burst pool for the worst offender and monitor.
capacity-bot: autoscaler triggered: +2 nodes in dedicated-eu-west-1c (reason: gpu_mem_pressure) — 1772504980
deploy-bot: canary rollback executed for tenant-7 batch job (reason: repeated allocation failures) — 1772505150
lee: keep an eye on cost delta; we should capture per-tenant cost for any burst migration to present to finance.
ana: noted — I'll add a short dashboard tile with estimated burst-hours/cost.
priya: FYI I’ll add a sanity eval to flag long-sequence jobs that look like they will blow up memory (heuristic based on seq_len * batch_size). If we catch earlier we can recommend quantization or chunking.
josh: cool. If this buys time we can avoid changing the eviction policy globally. Also let's avoid increasing hard-eviction aggressiveness — that burns customers.
ana: agreed. I'll start the migrator run and post results here in ~30m. :eyes: 
priya: thanks — ping me if you see the same pattern in ap-south, I'll schedule similar policy patch. :+1:
